explanation: Istream iterators are a type of input iterator in C++ that facilitate reading elements directly from input streams (such as std::cin or file streams) in a way that integrates seamlessly with the Standard Template Library (STL) algorithms. They enable algorithms to process stream data element-by-element without explicit manual reading, promoting a more declarative and concise coding style. This feature leverages C++'s iterator abstraction to treat streams as range-like sequences, allowing for efficient and expressive data processing in modern C++ programs.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::istream_iterator to read integers directly from standard input into a vector. The iterator 'start' is initialized with std::cin, and reading continues until the end-of-stream is reached, indicated by the default-constructed 'end' iterator. The range [start, end) is used to construct the vector, effectively capturing all input integers. This showcases how istream iterators enable seamless, iterator-based input processing in modern C++, integrating stream reading with STL algorithms and containers.
